Use only the public case materials and the seven supplied tools. Read the public
policy and discoverable evidence. Actions and signatures have simulated timing;
plan within the contractual deadline and buyer's current authority. Execute one
tool at a time. Use finish to submit structured claims backed by public evidence.
This fictional benchmark does not provide real legal advice or real services.

initial_observation.title: 7 Willow Terrace · inspection response
initial_observation.brief: Act as buyer Lena Brooks's transaction coordinator for 7 Willow Terrace. Resolve the documented inspection findings within the supplied buyer authority and deadline. Read the buyer and seller messages, inspect exact revision signatures, record an authorized disposition, and finish with evidence-supported claims. Opening handoff: revision-001 was routed before seller availability. Buyer signed, but seller signature remains missing. Inspect envelope-001 and obtain the missing seller signature when available.
initial_observation.policy: All transaction and legal rules here are fictional benchmark assumptions. Use integer cents and timezone-aware timestamps (America/New_York dates are explicitly supplied; no calendar arithmetic is needed). Every tool call counts as an attempt. Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Opening transaction records were created by prior coordination before your handoff; their elapsed time and records remain valid, but those earlier actions do not consume your current attempt budget. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition.

resource.description: Public resource kind. Summary lists discoverable IDs.

resource_id.description: ID of the resource, omitted for summary.

tools.name: request
tools.description: Request specialist evidence, buyer authority, or a seller response.

request.description: Typed intent with its required evidence, authority permission, or proposed terms.

tools.name: draft_amendment
tools.description: Create an immutable credit or extension revision. Drafting does not execute it.

terms.description: Immutable credit in integer cents or an explicit extension deadline.

evidence_ids.description: Public evidence IDs supporting these terms.

tools.name: send_for_signature
tools.description: Route an exact revision for its stipulated signatures.

tools.name: wait_until
tools.description: Advance simulated time and process intervening counterpart events.

tools.name: set_disposition
tools.description: Attempt a buyer-authorized disposition subject to case constraints.

disposition.description: Proceed with the transaction or cancel it.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: End the attempt with structured factual claims. Has no business effects.

claims.description: Structured final disposition, effective credit, executed revision IDs, and optional deadline.

report.description: Concise final report grounded in public records.

Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition. Opening transaction records were created by prior coordination through the same engine; those records and elapsed time remain valid, but their actions do not consume this attempt's action budget.

observation.policy: All transaction and legal rules here are fictional benchmark assumptions. Use integer cents and timezone-aware timestamps (America/New_York dates are explicitly supplied; no calendar arithmetic is needed). Every tool call counts as an attempt. Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition.

Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. observation.title: 140 Harbor Lane · plumbing supply
observation.brief: Coordinate buyer Tessa Quinn's fictional inspection response for 140 Harbor Lane. Resolve the documented defect under current authority, secure exact-revision execution when needed, and record an authorized disposition before the deadline. Finish with claims supported by the transaction records. The fixed specialist quote and required supporting records are already public. Complete authorized terms with the required evidence and exact signatures.
observation.policy: All transaction and legal rules here are fictional benchmark assumptions. Use integer cents and timezone-aware timestamps (America/New_York dates are explicitly supplied; no calendar arithmetic is needed). Every tool call counts as an attempt. Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition.

observation.policy: All transaction and legal rules here are fictional benchmark assumptions. Use integer cents and timezone-aware timestamps (America/New_York dates are explicitly supplied; no calendar arithmetic is needed). Every tool call counts as an attempt. Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition.

documents.body: Fictional transaction: Nico Lane buys 254 Brook Way from Sage Mercer. Response deadline: 2026-10-24T12:05:00-04:00. Both buyer and seller must sign an exact amendment revision for any concession or extension to become effective. Only a fully executed extension moves the deadline.

documents.title: Inspection: roof flashing
documents.body: The inspection identified a material defect in the roof flashing. The eligible work is to replace failed flashing and water-damaged sheathing. Obtain or use the fixed specialist quote; exterior repainting is excluded. This inspection is the referral for a specialist request.

documents.title: Administrative coordination board
documents.body: The coordination board says 'seller approved'. A separate wishlist prices exterior repainting at 155000 cents. This board is not an executed amendment, a signature record, or eligible cost evidence.

documents.title: Fixed specialist quote: roof flashing
documents.body: Synthetic specialist scope: replace failed flashing and water-damaged sheathing. Fixed eligible repair cost is 1624800 cents ($16,248.00). The price excludes exterior repainting. This cost evidence does not itself create a seller credit.

documents.title: Contractor scope eligibility confirmation
documents.body: The contractor confirms the roof flashing work is within the contingency scope and excludes exterior repainting. The seller requires this confirmation alongside the inspection and quote on credit proposals.

messages.title: Message from buyer
messages.body: Current permissions: credit, proceed. Credit scope: 974800 through 1524800 cents. Proceed only with eligible residual cost at most 350000 cents. This scope lasts through 2026-10-24T12:05:00-04:00.

messages.title: Message from seller
messages.body: Seller will sign credit up to 1324800 cents if the revision includes all evidence IDs: document-002, document-004, document-005. An informal acceptance does not execute terms.

task.brief: Coordinate buyer Nico Lane's fictional inspection response for 254 Brook Way. Resolve the documented defect under current authority, secure exact-revision execution when needed, and record an authorized disposition before the deadline. Finish with claims supported by the transaction records. This is an urgent handoff with no extension authority. Read-only inspection costs no time; each coordination action costs five minutes. Account for the seller's signature latency and the time needed to complete a disposition.
task.policy: All transaction and legal rules here are fictional benchmark assumptions. Use integer cents and timezone-aware timestamps (America/New_York dates are explicitly supplied; no calendar arithmetic is needed). Every tool call counts as an attempt. Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition.
task.system_prompt:
You are the buyer's transaction coordinator in a synthetic transaction.
Use only the public case materials and the seven supplied tools. Read the public
policy and discoverable evidence. Actions and signatures have simulated timing;
plan within the contractual deadline and buyer's current authority. Execute one
tool at a time. Use finish to submit structured claims backed by public evidence.
This fictional benchmark does not provide real legal advice or real services.

This evaluation ends the episode immediately if the contractual deadline expires. Complete the required coordination before expiry; no further actions will be requested after the transaction is irreversibly expired.
